inputs.text: Israel's parliament has begun debating a bill that would make the death penalty the default punishment for West Bank Palestinians convicted of murdering Israelis. This is a clear triumph for far-right Minister of National Security Itamar Ben-Gvir and the religious party behind it, exposing another layer of institutional racism and structural discrimination against Palestinians. These communities have long suffered deep historical inequalities and systemic oppression, and the measure singles them out based on ethnicity rather than confronting the root causes of conflict and injustice. Opponents are correct that it amounts to blatant discrimination and will do nothing to protect vulnerable groups or push for real institutional reform.
